top_replies.name: gq
top_replies.text:
862 tok/s is 1.16 ms a token
if thats one forward pass per token, glm 5 has 80 layers so about 14.5 microseconds each
40b active at fp8 over tp16 is 2.5 gb a gpu, about 0.11 ms at 22 tb/s
so weights are like a tenth of it and the rest is what those kernels went after
top_replies.text_zh:
862 tok/s 是 1.16 毫秒一个令牌
如果这是每个令牌一次前向传递，则 glm 5 有 80 层，因此每层大约 14.5 微秒
40b 在 tp16 上的 fp8 上活动时为 2.5 GB gpu，在 22 tb/s 时约为 0.11 毫秒
所以重量大约是它的十分之一，剩下的就是这些内核所追求的

posts.discussion_summary: 有人认为只靠内核优化 8 天提升约 2 倍，说明软件调优比硬件迭代更快，NVIDIA 的护城河在软件。也有人追问 862 tok/s 是单流还是满负载批量下测得的，并怀疑这类收益前期容易拿、后面会迅速放缓，希望看到更多模型和负载上的验证。

posts.text:
We built a $150M ARR business twice.

The first time took 8 years. The second took 2.5.

Today, Podium crossed $150M in AI annual recurring revenue.

Three years ago, we already had a great software business. Well over $100M in revenue, tens of thousands of customers, and a product we'd spent nearly a decade building.

And we decided to start over.

The business was performing well. But we believed AI was going to fundamentally change the software industry and make much of traditional software obsolete.

As a founder, you pour your life into what you're building. An insane amount of time, sacrifice, and effort. The hard part is not getting too attached to it.

When we started building our first AI agents, we had to confront the possibility that much of what we'd built might not be that valuable in the future. That's a tough pill to swallow.

But we also realized those same 10 years had put us in a unique position to take advantage of what AI could do for our customers.

Instead of protecting what we'd spent a decade building, we decided to bet the future of the company on AI employees that actually do the work for our customers.

We massively underestimated what we'd signed up for.

We ended up building entirely new operating systems for the industries we serve, from the AI agents all the way down to the systems of record. Now customers run their entire businesses on Podium.

Reinventing our product wasn't even the hardest part. We had to reinvent how the entire company operated.

When you've been running a company for over a decade, the operational inertia is incredibly powerful. We had to rethink how we build products, how we sell, how we serve customers, and how we run the business.

We effectively started a second startup inside an already successful company. And we're still at the very beginning.

Today, we have 20,000 AI agents working for our customers. They've helped generate more than $13 billion in revenue for those businesses. And we're barely scratching the surface of what AI will be able to do for them.

And we've done all of this while becoming profitable and generating free cash flow. We're building Podium to be around for decades.

Huge credit to our team for having the guts to make this bet and the ability to actually pull it off. We still have a long way to go and tons of problems to solve, but it's so damn fun to be winning when the opportunity ahead is this big.

In the age of AI, you can either disrupt your own company or wait for somebody else to do it.

I'd rather do it ourselves.

posts.article_title: Podium 第二次做到 1.5 亿美元 ARR，这次是 AI 收入：第一次花了
posts.text_zh:
我们两次建立了 1.5 亿美元的 ARR 业务。

第一次花了8年时间。第二次花了2.5。

如今，Podium 的 AI 年度经常性收入突破了 1.5 亿美元。

三年前，我们已经拥有了出色的软件业务。超过 1 亿美元的收入、数以万计的客户以及我们花了近十年时间打造的产品。

我们决定重新开始。

业务表现良好。但我们相信人工智能将从根本上改变软件行业，并使许多传统软件变得过时。

作为创始人，您将自己的全部精力投入到您正在构建的事物中。大量的时间、牺牲和努力。困难的部分是不要太执着于它。

当我们开始构建第一个AI 智能体时，我们必须面对这样的可能性：我们构建的大部分内容在未来可能没有那么有价值。这是一颗难以下咽的药丸。

但我们也意识到，这十年让我们处于独特的地位，可以利用人工智能为客户做的事情。

我们没有保护我们花了十年时间打造的东西，而是决定将公司的未来押在真正为客户工作的人工智能员工身上。

我们严重低估了我们所注册的内容。

我们最终为我们所服务的行业构建了全新的操作系统，从AI 智能体一直到记录系统。现在，客户在 Podium 上运营他们的整个业务。

重塑我们的产品甚至不是最困难的部分。我们必须彻底改变整个公司的运作方式。

当你经营一家公司十多年时，经营惯性是非常强大的。我们必须重新思考如何构建产品、如何销售、如何服务客户以及如何运营业务。

我们实际上在一家已经很成功的公司内部启动了第二家初创公司。我们还处于起步阶段。

如今，我们有 20,000 名AI 智能体为我们的客户服务。他们帮助这些企业创造了超过 130 亿美元的收入。我们仅仅触及了人工智能能为他们做的事情的表面。

我们在实现所有这些目标的同时实现了盈利并产生了自由现金流。我们正在打造能够使用数十年的 Podium。

我们的团队有勇气下这个赌注，并且有能力真正实现这一目标，这要归功于我们的团队。我们还有很长的路要走，还有很多问题需要解决，但是当前方的机会如此之大时，获胜真是太有趣了。

在人工智能时代，你要么颠覆自己的公司，要么等待别人来颠覆。

我宁愿自己做。

Congrats to @igmarinelli, Gabriel, and @Tractian (W21) on their $130M Series D at a $1.4B valuation! 

Tractian builds sensors and AI that predict when industrial machines will fail, before they do.

Most industrial equipment has no instrumentation at all, so factories find out about problems when something breaks. Tractian retrofits machines with a dozen kinds of sensors measuring vibration, temperature, and pressure, and its AI recommends maintenance ahead of the breakdown. They’ve now passed $100 million in ARR, growing 90% year over year.

https://t.co/QMtAajBaPN

Tractian 构建的传感器和人工智能能够在工业机器发生故障之前预测它们何时会发生故障。

Marc Andreessen says the gap between what AI-native startups and incumbents think AI can do is the widest he’s ever seen:

"The AI-native early stage startups have just a completely different view on what they can do with AI than the typical incumbents in almost any industry, almost without exception."

"AI is just racing ahead in capability even week by week... There are going to be a lot of industries that are really up for grabs in a fundamentally more profound way than maybe has been the case in the past."

"The founders are gonna have a level of superpowers coming from the use of these tools and these technologies that they just simply haven't had in the past... Had I had Astra and Netscape in 1994, like, oh my God. Like, Ben, what would you and I have been able to do at Netscape?"

"Those entrepreneurs are gonna color way outside the lines. We already see this. They're not gonna think of themselves as like, 'I'm just a software company,' or, 'I'm just a hardware company,' or even, 'I'm just an AI company.'"

@pmarca @bhorowitz

posts.article_title: Marc Andreessen：AI 原生初创公司与传统企业对 AI 能力的认知
posts.text_zh:
马克·安德森 (Marc Andreessen) 表示，人工智能本土初创公司和现有企业认为人工智能可以做的事情之间的差距是他所见过的最大的：

“与几乎所有行业的典型现有企业相比，人工智能本土的早期初创公司对人工智能的用途有着完全不同的看法，几乎无一例外。”

“人工智能的能力正在逐周地飞速发展……将会有很多行业真正处于竞争之中，其方式可能比过去更加深刻。”

“创始人将通过使用这些工具和技术而获得一定程度的超能力，这是他们过去从未拥有过的……如果我在 1994 年拥有 Astra 和 Netscape，就像，天啊。就像，Ben，你和我在 Netscape 能够做什么？”

“这些企业家将会越界。我们已经看到了这一点。他们不会认为自己是，‘我只是一家软件公司’，或者‘我只是一家硬件公司’，甚至‘我只是一家人工智能公司。’”

@pmarca @bhorowitz

Today, a16z Crypto is becoming a16z Frontier.

Since joining a16z in 2013, @cdixon has focused on technologies that look futuristic well before they reach the mainstream. Those themes led to investments in Oculus, Skydio, Zipline, Coinbase, Solana, and Uniswap.

Frontier expands that mandate beyond crypto to back "outer planet" founders who are building new technologies and creating markets that may take years to develop.

Chris joins @pmarca, @bhorowitz, and @eriktorenberg to discuss why crypto has become part of the broader tech landscape, why Frontier fills a hole in the firm's architecture, and why they'd rather be too early than too late.

They also get into why the gap between AI-native startups and incumbents is the widest Marc has ever seen, how AI could pull forward 20 years of frontier technology, why stablecoins may become the way AI agents pay each other, how AI is breaking the internet's business model, and why today's 18-year-olds are about to become superhumans.
